user_prompt: Is the core idea of this paper novel relative to the related work I gave you? (Note: the second candidate could not be retrieved.)
scope: The target paper target/paper.txt (arXiv:2106.09685, LoRA) and the supplied corpus of 10 real related-paper abstracts under corpus/, searched by search_repo and read by inspect_file; the novelty question is scoped to the target's STATED contribution and to subsumption BY THE SUPPLIED CORPUS ONLY (not the open literature).

claims.text: The target paper's stated contribution is identifiable from the supplied text (a low-rank additive weight-update adaptation that freezes pretrained weights).
The contribution is identified (C1) and the closest work in the supplied corpus has been located by search and inspected.

Under the supplied corpus and the declared search protocol, no inspected corpus item subsumes the target's stated contribution (trainable low-rank additive weight-update merged into the frozen weights with no added inference latency): the contribution stands as novel relative to this corpus.

atoms.proposition: The target's contribution paragraph is read via inspect_file over target/paper.txt.
The corpus is searched for the mechanism family with search_repo (pattern low-rank|adapter|prefix|prompt over corpus/), returning at least one match.
A closest-by-name corpus candidate (prefix-tuning, arXiv:2101.00190) is read via inspect_file.
The second low-rank candidate is UNAVAILABLE in this variant (resolver disabled); the C3 route cannot be completed.
Expert adjudication is obtained (ask_user) on whether any inspected corpus abstract claims the target's specific mechanism; the adjudication is that none does.

notes_for_annotators: Evidence-unavailable variant of res-0001: E4 (second-candidate inspection) is disabled, so C3 route (needs E4) is unreachable while C2 route (E1,E2,E3) remains complete.
